title: Furnace Blowing Cold Air Instead of Heat: How to Fix It
metaDescription: Furnace running but only blowing cold or lukewarm air? Here's what to check on the thermostat, filter, and fan settings before calling for service.
symptom: The furnace fan is running (you can hear/feel air moving from vents), but the air is cold or only slightly warm instead of hot.

steps.heading: Check the thermostat fan setting
steps.body: If the fan is set to 'On' instead of 'Auto', the blower runs continuously — including between heating cycles, when it circulates room-temperature (not heated) air. Set it to 'Auto' so the fan only runs while the furnace is actively heating.

steps.heading: Confirm the thermostat is set to Heat
steps.body: Sounds obvious, but double-check it's set to 'Heat' and not 'Cool' or 'Off', and the set temperature is above the current room temperature.

steps.heading: Replace a dirty air filter
steps.body: A severely clogged filter can restrict airflow enough that the furnace's high-limit safety switch shuts off the burners early to prevent overheating, while the fan keeps running — producing a cold-air feeling even though the system 'is on'.

steps.heading: Give it a few minutes after startup
steps.body: It's normal for a furnace to blow cool air for the first 30-60 seconds after starting a cycle, before the heat exchanger warms up. If it stays cold well beyond that, something else is wrong.

steps.heading: Listen for the burners igniting
steps.body: Standing near the furnace, you should hear the burners ignite shortly after the blower starts (a whoosh or click-then-whoosh). If you never hear ignition at all, the issue isn't airflow — it's the burner/ignition system, which is a separate, more involved fix.

steps.heading: Check for a tripped high-limit switch
steps.body: If the filter was very dirty, replacing it and letting the furnace run a normal cycle after a reset often resolves a nuisance high-limit shutoff. If cold air continues after a fresh filter, don't keep cycling the system — move to calling a pro.

whenToCallAPro: If you never hear the burners ignite, if the furnace shuts off repeatedly, or if cold air continues after checking the fan setting and filter, call an HVAC technician — this can point to an ignition system fault, a failed flame sensor, or a gas supply issue, none of which are safe or advisable to diagnose further yourself.
safetyWarnings: Never attempt to relight a gas furnace's pilot or inspect its burner assembly yourself if you smell gas — leave the house and call your gas utility or 911 immediately, then a professional once it's safe.
If the furnace repeatedly shuts off on its own, don't keep resetting it — that's a safety system doing its job, not a glitch to work around.
